cells.tense: Right now you can sit with what you feel without needing to rush it into anything, and that steadiness is yours.
cells.ask: When something real arrives today, follow it one layer deeper before you decide what it means — let the understanding come to you rather than reaching for it.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you're meeting it with a settled heart. You can feel what's true without needing to act on it yet, and in the middle of all that you can also tell where you end and the other person begins. That isn't a mood that happens to be passing through. It's how you're receiving things right now, and it changes what you're able to notice.

So when something real comes in today, stay with it one beat past the point where you'd normally start naming it. Let what's arriving take you into its own depth before you go looking for a meaning to put on top. The shape will show itself if you give it room.
cells.sheetLine: Something real is arriving and you can receive it without rushing — let it take you one layer deeper.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before anything moves
cells.place: at the threshold where what was outside is arriving now

cells.tense: You're already feeling how this will land before it has arrived, bracing for a connection that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: When you sense something coming toward you, let it arrive half-finished and wait for it to complete itself — the ending it grows into will be truer than the one you're rehearsing.
cells.core:
When this is going well, what's entering meets a heart that's already steady. You take things in as they come, you let a feeling be what it is in its own time, and closeness to someone doesn't cost you your own footing. That's the place you're working from. It's just not the place you're standing in today.

What's arriving, you've already felt ahead of schedule. The ending is written before the first line lands. The bracing is doing the feeling's job, and so the feeling never gets to arrive on its own — it shows up already decided. Let the thing come unfinished. Wait for the shape it actually grows into.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling what's coming before it arrives — let it land before you decide what it means.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before anything moves
cells.place: at the threshold where what was outside is arriving now

cells.tense: You stopped letting things reach you and you're still standing where you stopped, not arriving in what's here.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding at a distance — a person, a feeling, a moment — and gather your thoughts around it until you can see it clearly enough to say what it actually is.
cells.core:
When this is going well, what's entering finds you open and settled at once. You can be moved by something without being swept off your feet, and you can let another person close without the closeness costing you your own shape. That's what receiving looks like when it's working. Right now the receiving has gone quiet.

What's arriving is at the threshold and hasn't come any further, because watching from a step back got comfortable. Not because nothing's there. Sit with the thing you've been keeping at arm's length and let your thinking line up around what it really is — one clean read, nothing more than that. That's enough for the door.
cells.sheetLine: Something is arriving and you're watching from behind the threshold — gather your thoughts and step through.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before anything moves

cells.tense: You're already receiving what arrives and knowing it deeply, and you'd say it's just something that happens to you.
cells.ask: When something moves you today, stay with it past the first wave — go deeper into what it's actually showing you, and name what you find as yours.
cells.core:
Going well, this is steady closeness you can feel in your body and hold in your own hands. Something arrives, it settles into you, and you know it's yours — the warmth is yours, the seeing is yours. That's the capacity you're running on right now. You're using it the whole time.

What's missing is only that you describe the receiving as though it arrived without you. It came in, it moved through, that's simply how it goes. The capacity is working; the ownership of it hasn't been picked up. Go deeper than the first wave and let it show you the pattern underneath, then say out loud that you're the one who sees it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already letting things land and knowing them — follow it deeper and claim what you see.
